answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to place a bond in a shared escrow before it can submit work. The protocol releases the bond only after independent reviewers validate the result; proven duplicate or collusive identities forfeit it. This does not make fake identities impossible, but makes each one costly: an attacker must lock capital across many accounts and risks losing it when caught. A low-value task tagged ember, crystal, or willow still faces the same bond rule.
